comment: The entry-point typology takes the country as the unit of analysis. In devolved health systems this conceals the binding constraint: intra-national heterogeneity. The Philippines is squarely Entry Point 2 nationally (integrating existing systems), yet a large share of its 1,400+ municipalities — where surveillance operating capacity actually sits post-devolution — are functionally at Entry Point 1, with epidemiology and surveillance units that are designation-based (existing RHU staff deputised by executive order) rather than resourced, and without dedicated connectivity or hardware budgets. National-level classification will misdirect sequencing and investment in any devolved system (Philippines, Indonesia, Kenya, Nigeria).

public.text: The entry-point typology takes the country as the unit of analysis. In devolved health systems this conceals the binding constraint: intra-national heterogeneity. The Philippines is squarely Entry Point 2 nationally (integrating existing systems), yet a large share of its 1,400+ municipalities — where surveillance operating capacity actually sits post-devolution — are functionally at Entry Point 1, with epidemiology and surveillance units that are designation-based (existing RHU staff deputised by executive order) rather than resourced, and without dedicated connectivity or hardware budgets. National-level classification will misdirect sequencing and investment in any devolved system (Philippines, Indonesia, Kenya, Nigeria).
public.suggestedRevision: Add a sub-national tiering paragraph to 4.2.1: countries should classify entry points at the level at which health services are governed and financed, and the national roadmap should provide differentiated pathways for sub-national units at different entry points, including a floor package for the least-resourced tier.
